title: Time and Place Words in Retelling

sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know *al día siguiente*, *aquel día* and *el día anterior* from B1 Unit 38, and *aquí* → *allí* and *mañana* → *al día siguiente* from B1 Unit 33. You know *este*, *ese* and *aquel* from A1 Unit 11. The idea behind all of them is the same: time and place words point from where the speaker stands. When you retell, you stand somewhere else, so they change. This lesson gives the full list and says when they do not change.

sections.title: What was said → what you retell
New: venir becomes ir
sections.content: *Venir* and *ir* depend on where you stand when you retell. Ana says from her house: «Ven a mi casa mañana.» If you retell it somewhere else, you say *Me dijo que fuera a su casa al día siguiente*. If you retell it at her house, *venir* stays: *Me dijo que viniera al día siguiente*.

sections.title: New: when the words stay
sections.content: If you retell on the same day and in the same place, nothing has to change. Ana said this morning: «Llego hoy.» At noon, in the same office, you say *Dijo que llegaba hoy*. Only the verb moves back.

items.spanish: Ana dijo que estaría allí al día siguiente.
items.english: Ana said that she would be there the next day.

items.spanish: Me contó que aquella semana había estado muy ocupada.
items.english: She told me that she had been very busy that week.

items.spanish: Me dijo que fuera a su casa al día siguiente.
items.english: She told me to go to her house the next day.
He said that he was arriving today. (Said the same day.)

sections.content: Before you retell, ask yourself three things: when am I speaking, where am I, and who am I speaking to? If the answers are the same as in the original, keep the words. If not, move them.
